question.:question/problem:
Evaluate the integral. Give an exact answer.

$$
\int_{0}^{\frac{1}{10}} \frac{5}{\sqrt{1 - 25 x^{2}}}\,\mathrm{d}x
$$

{{answer}}
question.:question/worked-solution:
Use the linear substitution $u=5 x.$ Then

$$
\frac{\mathrm{d}u}{\mathrm{d}x}=5,\qquad \mathrm{d}x=(\frac{1}{5})\,\mathrm{d}u.
$$

Change both bounds using the same substitution:

$$
\begin{aligned}x=0&\Longrightarrow u=(5)(0)=0 \\ x=\frac{1}{10}&\Longrightarrow u=(5)(\frac{1}{10})=\frac{1}{2}\end{aligned}
$$

Both transformed endpoints lie strictly between $-1$ and $1$, so the integrand is continuous throughout the interval.

Apply the basic inverse-trigonometric integral:

$$
\int \frac{1}{\sqrt{1-u^{2}}}\,\mathrm{d}u=\operatorname{arcsin}{\left(u \right)}+C.
$$

Substitute and evaluate:

$$
\begin{aligned}\int_{0}^{\frac{1}{10}} \frac{5}{\sqrt{1 - 25 x^{2}}}\,\mathrm{d}x &= 5\int_{0}^{\frac{1}{10}} \frac{1}{\sqrt{1-(5 x)^{2}}}\,\mathrm{d}x \\  &= 5(\frac{1}{5})\int_{0}^{\frac{1}{2}} \frac{1}{\sqrt{1-u^{2}}}\,\mathrm{d}u \\  &= 1\int_{0}^{\frac{1}{2}} \frac{1}{\sqrt{1-u^{2}}}\,\mathrm{d}u \\  &= 1[\operatorname{arcsin}{\left(u \right)}]_{0}^{\frac{1}{2}} \\  &= 1(\operatorname{arcsin}(\frac{1}{2})-\operatorname{arcsin}(0)) \\  &= 1((\frac{\pi}{6})-(0)) \\  &= \frac{\pi}{6}\end{aligned}
$$

question.:question/problem:
Evaluate the integral. Give an exact answer.

$$
\int_{0}^{\frac{1}{5}} \frac{5}{25 x^{2} + 1}\,\mathrm{d}x
$$

{{answer}}
question.:question/worked-solution:
Use the linear substitution $u=5 x.$ Then

$$
\frac{\mathrm{d}u}{\mathrm{d}x}=5,\qquad \mathrm{d}x=(\frac{1}{5})\,\mathrm{d}u.
$$

Change both bounds using the same substitution:

$$
\begin{aligned}x=0&\Longrightarrow u=(5)(0)=0 \\ x=\frac{1}{5}&\Longrightarrow u=(5)(\frac{1}{5})=1\end{aligned}
$$

Apply the basic inverse-trigonometric integral:

$$
\int \frac{1}{1+u^{2}}\,\mathrm{d}u=\operatorname{arctan}{\left(u \right)}+C.
$$

Substitute and evaluate:

$$
\begin{aligned}\int_{0}^{\frac{1}{5}} \frac{5}{25 x^{2} + 1}\,\mathrm{d}x &= 5\int_{0}^{\frac{1}{5}} \frac{1}{1+(5 x)^{2}}\,\mathrm{d}x \\  &= 5(\frac{1}{5})\int_{0}^{1} \frac{1}{1+u^{2}}\,\mathrm{d}u \\  &= 1\int_{0}^{1} \frac{1}{1+u^{2}}\,\mathrm{d}u \\  &= 1[\operatorname{arctan}{\left(u \right)}]_{0}^{1} \\  &= 1(\operatorname{arctan}(1)-\operatorname{arctan}(0)) \\  &= 1((\frac{\pi}{4})-(0)) \\  &= \frac{\pi}{4}\end{aligned}
$$

question.:question/problem:
Evaluate the integral. Give an exact answer.

$$
\int_{0}^{\frac{5 \sqrt{2}}{2}} \frac{5}{\sqrt{25 - x^{2}}}\,\mathrm{d}x
$$

{{answer}}
question.:question/worked-solution:
First factor the constant in the denominator:

$$
\sqrt{25 - x^{2}}=\sqrt{25(1-(\frac{1}{25})x^{2})}
$$

Use the linear substitution $u=\frac{x}{5}.$ Then

$$
\frac{\mathrm{d}u}{\mathrm{d}x}=\frac{1}{5},\qquad \mathrm{d}x=(5)\,\mathrm{d}u.
$$

Change both bounds using the same substitution:

$$
\begin{aligned}x=0&\Longrightarrow u=(\frac{1}{5})(0)=0 \\ x=\frac{5 \sqrt{2}}{2}&\Longrightarrow u=(\frac{1}{5})(\frac{5 \sqrt{2}}{2})=\frac{\sqrt{2}}{2}\end{aligned}
$$

Both transformed endpoints lie strictly between $-1$ and $1$, so the integrand is continuous throughout the interval.

Apply the basic inverse-trigonometric integral:

$$
\int \frac{1}{\sqrt{1-u^{2}}}\,\mathrm{d}u=\operatorname{arcsin}{\left(u \right)}+C.
$$

Substitute and evaluate:

$$
\begin{aligned}\int_{0}^{\frac{5 \sqrt{2}}{2}} \frac{5}{\sqrt{25 - x^{2}}}\,\mathrm{d}x &= 1\int_{0}^{\frac{5 \sqrt{2}}{2}} \frac{1}{\sqrt{1-(\frac{x}{5})^{2}}}\,\mathrm{d}x \\  &= 1(5)\int_{0}^{\frac{\sqrt{2}}{2}} \frac{1}{\sqrt{1-u^{2}}}\,\mathrm{d}u \\  &= 5\int_{0}^{\frac{\sqrt{2}}{2}} \frac{1}{\sqrt{1-u^{2}}}\,\mathrm{d}u \\  &= 5[\operatorname{arcsin}{\left(u \right)}]_{0}^{\frac{\sqrt{2}}{2}} \\  &= 5(\operatorname{arcsin}(\frac{\sqrt{2}}{2})-\operatorname{arcsin}(0)) \\  &= 5((\frac{\pi}{4})-(0)) \\  &= \frac{5 \pi}{4}\end{aligned}
$$
